title: Working Backward from Verified AI Model Evaluation: What Would Cryptographic Proof of AI Evaluation Require?

original_idea.body:
# Working Backward from Verified AI Model Evaluation: What Would Cryptographic Proof of AI Evaluation Require?

**Problem:** RAND's Sarma & Fisher (2026) propose using formal methods to cryptographically prove AI models underwent approved evaluations without tampering — enabling credible verification in international AI governance agreements. The technical requirements for this are undefined.

**Direction:** Define a minimal technical stack for a 'verified AI evaluation protocol': (1) formal specification of evaluation procedure, (2) cryptographic commitment to model weights, (3) proof of evaluation execution. Identify each technical component's current readiness level. Estimate which components are 10-year vs. 2-year problems.

**Why it matters:** This is a critical governance application of formal methods to AI safety. If the technical components exist, deployment planning can begin. If they do not, early-stage research can be motivated by this concrete goal.

**Relevant context:** RAND (2026) proposes this as a future direction. Zero-knowledge proofs (SNARKs, STARKs) could provide the cryptographic component. Lean 4 could provide the formal specification. No synthesis of these components has been proposed.
